classifications.rationale: The President directs the Secretary of Agriculture and Forest Service to manage, protect, restore, delineate, and report the boundaries of the groves; these are ongoing administrative and land-management actions, with no substantive legal consequence performed by this segment itself.
classifications.evidence: The Secretary of Agriculture is directed to delineate the location of such Giant Sequoia groves

classifications.rationale: This segment inseparably combines a mandated later agency legal outcome—Interior must withdraw the groves from mineral-location and leasing regimes—with present, self-executing prohibitions on timber management and inclusion in the allowable-sale land base.
classifications.evidence: The designated Giant Sequoia groves shall not be managed for timber production

classifications.rationale: The President assigns the Secretary of Agriculture ongoing management duties concerning proposed development and the Converse Basin Grove; any implementation occurs through later agency management, while the final sentence disclaims enforceable private rights.
classifications.evidence: the Secretary of Agriculture shall assure that any proposed development shall provide for aesthetic, recreational, ecological, and scientific value
